title: How the spine supports movement and protects nerves
intro: The spine is a chain of bones, joints and discs supported by muscles and ligaments. It carries load while protecting the spinal cord and nerve roots. Its normal curves are part of its design, not proof of poor posture.

sections.heading: Regions
paragraphs: The neck, chest and lower back have different movement and loading patterns. The sacrum links the spine to the pelvis; fused lower bones move differently from the mobile vertebrae above.

sections.heading: Discs and joints
paragraphs: Discs distribute load between most vertebral bodies. Small facet joints guide movement. Age-related changes on a scan are common and do not automatically explain pain or require surgery.

sections.heading: Nerve space
paragraphs: The spinal canal and side openings allow neural structures to pass. Irritation or compression can cause radiating pain, numbness or weakness; symptom location and examination help interpretation.

sections.heading: Daily movement
paragraphs: Vary positions, maintain tolerable activity and build strength gradually. No single posture prevents all back pain. After major trauma, avoid unnecessary movement and seek appropriate emergency care.

sections.heading: Warning signs
paragraphs: New bladder or bowel dysfunction, saddle numbness or progressive leg weakness needs urgent assessment. Back pain with fever, major injury or concerning illness history also needs medical review rather than forceful manipulation.

A diagram explains typical structure, not the cause of an individual symptom. Before a consultation, note when a change began, what brings it on and how it affects daily activities. Bring previous results and ask how the findings fit together.

examples.title: A practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Mira sees degenerative wording on a scan. She asks how it fits her examination instead of assuming her back is fragile and stopping all activity.

examples.title: Another practical example
examples.text: In this hypothetical example, Arben develops numbness around the groin and new urinary difficulty. He seeks urgent care instead of waiting for routine physiotherapy.
